# Was the Bell MTS email outage a cyberattack?

**Reported.** Reported. Bell MTS told one outlet on Nov 22 that a cyberattack on its email provider, through a password-reset flaw, caused it. Earlier posts gave no cause. Scale and attacker not established.

Incident: Bell MTS email outage, Nov 2026. Also reported as Bell MTS email lockout and Manitoba Bell MTS email outage. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 7:11 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Bell MTS, Bell Canada, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 7:11 PM ET: **Bell MTS says a cyberattack caused its email outage. One outlet so far; Reported.** New incident page. Sources read: Winnipeg Free Press (Nov 22 and Nov 20), CBC (two stories), BleepingComputer, the Globe and Mail (Tier 2). Main question: Reported, because the Nov 22 statement reaches us through one outlet and Bell has not posted it on its own channels. The Bell Canada Nov 17 breach is covered here only as context; it is not on the site as its own page yet. Scale and attacker: Not established. Status monitoring. Privacy check done: no names, bylines, handles or contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. Bell MTS email customers across Manitoba were locked out for more than two days, per CBC and the Free Press. Bell has not said how many customers or accounts were affected, so size rests on reach, not a count.
- Who is affected: Bell MTS email customers in Manitoba, many locked out from about Nov 17 to Nov 20 and some for longer. Bell says it will contact customers whose data may have been affected.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 2+ days | Customers locked out of email | CBC, from customer accounts |
| Nov 22 | Bell names a cyberattack | To the Free Press |
| Nov 17 | Bell Canada breach date | Per Bell; separate system |

### Known so far

- Bell MTS email customers in Manitoba were locked out for days, and Bell said on Nov 20 that service was restored.
- Bell gave no cause for the outage until Nov 22.
- Bell says an agentic attacker stole enterprise customer data from its systems on Nov 17.
- Bell says it shared details with the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and is working with the RCMP's cybercrime unit.

### Not known yet

- Whether a second outlet or Bell's own notice carries the cyberattack statement.
- How many customers or accounts were affected, and what data was reachable.
- Who was behind it.
- Whether it is the same attack as Bell Canada's Nov 17 breach.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of our latest check.

- A Bell MTS or Bell Canada notice on its own site or channels saying a cyberattack caused the email outage. We read the statement through the Winnipeg Free Press only.
- A second outlet carrying the cyberattack statement. CBC's outage story (Nov 20, updated Nov 21) says Bell would not give a cause; we found no CBC or CTV follow-up. A CTV story was seen in search only and not read.
- The name of the third-party email provider.
- A count of affected customers or accounts, or the data types involved.
- Any claim of responsibility or attribution. We did not look at leak sites, underground forums or trackers.
- Any Bell or Canadian Centre for Cyber Security statement linking the email outage to the Bell Canada breach of Nov 17.
